blogs.title: A Smarter Way to Update Giant AI Models Without Retraining Them
blogs.description: This post introduces the big problem the paper tackles: how to adapt massive pretrained models to new tasks without paying the huge cost of full retraining. It explains parameter-efficient finetuning in plain language, compares common approaches like LoRA, adapters, and prompt tuning, and shows why the authors focus on changing a model with small, structured updates instead of rewriting all its weights.

blogs.title: Why 'Orthogonal Finetuning' Helps AI Learn New Tasks Without Forgetting Old Ones
blogs.description: This post focuses on the core idea of orthogonal finetuning. It explains how rotating a model's internal representations with orthogonal matrices helps preserve relationships between neurons, which can protect useful knowledge from pretraining. The article would translate the math into intuitive ideas like preserving angles, stability, and why this can lead to better generalization than more common low-rank update methods.

blogs.title: From Fast Fourier Transforms to Better AI Finetuning: The Butterfly Trick
blogs.description: This post centers on the paper's main innovation: using butterfly factorization, a structure inspired by the Fast Fourier Transform, to build dense but efficient orthogonal updates. It would explain how a clever sequence of small sparse transformations can act like a powerful full matrix while using far fewer trainable parameters, making the method both practical and elegant.

blogs.title: What Does Finetuning Have to Do With Information Flow? A Visual Guide to the Paper's Big Insight
blogs.description: This post explains the authors' information transmission view of matrix factorization. Instead of diving straight into formulas, it would use the metaphor of messages traveling through a network to show why some sparse patterns are too restrictive and why butterfly connections are more expressive. This makes the paper's theoretical contribution much easier for a general technical audience to understand.

blogs.title: BOFT vs. LoRA: Two Different Philosophies for Making Foundation Models Cheaper to Adapt
blogs.description: This post compares BOFT with LoRA in accessible terms. It highlights the difference between additive low-rank updates and multiplicative orthogonal updates, and discusses trade-offs in parameter count, expressiveness, stability, and inductive bias. Readers would come away with a practical understanding of when BOFT's structure-preserving approach might be more appealing than today's most popular finetuning method.

blogs.title: One Finetuning Method, Many AI Domains: How BOFT Works Across Language, Vision, and Image Generation
blogs.description: This post focuses on the paper's empirical results and why they matter. It shows that BOFT is not just a niche trick for one model type, but a general finetuning method tested on large language models, vision transformers, and text-to-image diffusion systems. The article would emphasize what this broad applicability says about the future of reusable, adaptable foundation models.
